To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the increase in pulmonary blood flow and decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance that accompany advancing gestational age in fetal lambs are due to an increased number of small pulmonary vessels and an increased amount of smooth muscle in the walls of these vessels.

the morphological development that accompany increasing pulmonary blood flow with advancing gestation is an increase in the number of vessels per lung and that the development that accompanies decreasing pulmonary vascular resistance is an increase in vasomotor reactivty related to an increase of the amount of smooth muscle per unit lung.

the morphological development that accompanied increasing pulmonary blood flow, and decreased pulmonary vascular reactivity with advancing gestational ages was due to an increase the total number of pulmonary vessels and increased vasodilator reactivity was related to an increase of the amount of smooth muscle in individual vessels while the thickness of smooth muscle remained constant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the morphologic development of the pulmonary arterial bed in fetal lambs from 85 days gestation to term.
the development of the pulmonary vascular bed and its response to increased blood flow.
the development of the pulmonary vascular bed and the relationship of that development to increasing pulmonary blood flow with advancing gestation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the increase in pulmonary blood flow and the decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance with increasing gestation are due in large part to an increase in pulmonary vascular bed and an increase in smooth muscle content of the vessels in the pulmonary vascular bed.

the morphological development that occurs with increasing pulmonary blood flow, decreasing vascular resistance, and increased reactivity of the pulmonary vascular bed in the fetal lamb is due to an increase of the total amount of vascular smooth muscle in the pulmonary vascular bed.
pulmonary vascular development is a complex process that is not completely understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pulmonary vascular bed of fetal lambs increases in size with increasing gestational ages and that the increase in size is due to an increase of the number of vessels and not an increase in their size.
the pulmonary vasculature is developing to accommodate increased blood flow and to maintain low resistance.
the pulmonary vasculature is a dynamic system that undergoes changes in the number of vessels as well as in the thickness of the muscular layer of individual vessels with advancing gestation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the pulmonary vascular resistance decreases with gestational age, which is a reflection of an increase in the number of pulmonary vessels, which in turn is a function of the increase in the total lung volume.

the increase in pulmonary blood flow and decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance with gestational age is not due to an increase the thickness of the medial smooth muscle of the pulmonary arteries, but rather an increase in the number of vessels and the amount of smooth muscle in the vessels.
there is no evidence for a decrease in medial smooth muscle mass in the resistance arteries with increasing gestation in the fetal lamb.
